key_insight: CMR-EXTR uses a teacher–student distillation pipeline to convert free-text CMR reports into auditable structured fields with per-field confidence scores, enabling lightweight, fully offline inference and reduced manual annotation.
problem_solved: Automates the conversion of unstructured cardiac MRI reports into reliable, auditable structured data — addressing bottlenecks in cohort assembly, longitudinal curation, and clinical decision support while preserving deployability and privacy.
method: Teacher–student distillation: a large LLM teacher generates labels/annotations to train a compact student model for offline deployment and reduced annotation burden.
Per-field uncertainty scoring: the system produces confidence estimates for each extracted field to enable quality control and selective human review.
Lightweight architecture optimized for fully offline inference, supporting clinical privacy and scalable cohort extraction without continuous cloud access.
impact: Enables scalable, privacy-preserving extraction of structured clinical data with built-in auditability; practitioners can deploy compact models in production settings while using confidence scores to prioritize human review and improve downstream analyses.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: free-text CMR report → LLM teacher (label generation) → distilled student model → structured fields + per-field confidence.
Before/after example: raw CMR sentence alongside extracted structured table with confidence tags (green/yellow/red).
Reliability chart: calibration plot or histogram showing confidence vs. actual accuracy to illustrate uncertainty utility.
Dashboard mockup: cohort view with filters and flagged low-confidence records for human curation.
paper_title: Uncertainty-Aware Structured Data Extraction from Full CMR Reports via Distilled LLMs
paper_authors: Yi Yu, Parker Martin, Zhenyu Bu, Yixuan Liu, Yi-Yu Zheng
